behavior_check_definitions.all_complete: all declared member rows exist and validate against their own T; for unforced_control, T is a completion budget and token values come only from actual raw greedy predictions
behavior_check_definitions.contextual_error: every expected error includes its frozen error_contains string; at least one error must be observed
behavior_check_definitions.count: successful call returns exactly one output per declared prompt, error calls return none
behavior_check_definitions.declared_mechanisms: for each unforced owner, all candidate required_mechanisms of the bound execution group are derived from its actual own-token execution events, not from case labels or fixed-prefix captures
behavior_check_definitions.execution_history: every actual input slice, position, effective length and sampled boundary matches prompt+continuation[:t] for fixed_prefix_execution, or prompt+actual own sampled/returned tokens[:t] for unforced_control
behavior_check_definitions.finished: every returned public output has finished=true
behavior_check_definitions.order: actual admission IDs are continuous across successful calls starting from zero; returned output IDs equal the admission ID list in order
behavior_check_definitions.prefix_ranges: first executed cached range for every member equals its explicit expected_cached_tokens; reused history is a prefix of a computed setup history; at least two distinct positive reuse lengths occur
behavior_check_definitions.recompute_observed: after at least one completion token was advanced, a real prefill execution overlaps a previously computed history interval; a prefill label or new-token-only prefix hit is insufficient
behavior_check_definitions.rejected_before_admission: every expected error has no output and no admission binding; next successful call preserves the continuous admission ID sequence
behavior_check_definitions.resolved_eos_stop: at least one ignore_eos=false call actually returns a resolved EOS as its last token strictly before max_tokens; reaching max_tokens with EOS does not prove early stopping
behavior_check_definitions.stop_policy: ignore_eos=true requires exactly max_tokens; otherwise require 1..max_tokens with no EOS before the last token, and last token is EOS unless max_tokens reached
behavior_check_definitions.waiting_admission: an actual execution event contains both a newly admitted request and a previously seen decoding request

protocol_rules.applicability: Reference requires actual prefill/decode/batch and identical logical history, never fake Rust scheduler events; baseline requires its own declared chunk/capacity/prefix evidence; candidate owns page/prefix/recompute/waiting coverage.
protocol_rules.fixed_prefix_rule: T frozen continuation tokens imply exactly T predictions; last advance is recorded but not computed; controls are separately counted unforced ignore-EOS T-row owners.
protocol_rules.behavior_rule: free_generation uses real EOS policy and no forcing; fixed_prefix_execution checks reuse explicitly identified real numerical captures and never claim free-generation evidence.
protocol_rules.threshold_rule: Fault differences and legal calibration outputs must be jointly reviewed; no budget is inferred, and no acceptance numerical output may be read before approval.
protocol_rules.eos_missing_rule: No actual early resolved EOS means required mechanism not covered: INVALID/blocks acceptance, not an inference-accuracy or EOS-state-machine diagnosis. An emitted EOS followed by a stop/length-policy violation is a behavior FAIL. Calibration may assess triggerability with a subsequent formal Definition change; never iteratively replace prompts after inspecting acceptance outcomes.
protocol_rules.unforced_control_rule: For each public prefix/pressure/waiting case, the candidate control and its fresh control-replay run every frozen setup and target public call with forcing disabled. Frozen continuation values are not advanced: only their lengths set max_tokens. Raw logits, own greedy advances, actual inputs/events and final ordered/detokenized RequestOutput values are saved. Public outputs must equal the sampled execution history. Both owners must satisfy actual mechanisms and bit-identical logits/returns. Existing control is shared with collection-equivalence evidence and counted once; all setup captures, receipts, guards, control-replay rows and public returns are marker dependencies.
protocol_rules.mandatory_cpu_regression: The public mixed_chunked_prefill_and_decode_survive_three_block_pressure regression remains required: prompt IDs 512 copies of1 and255 copies of2; T4/5; context768; token budget128; seqs2; three256-token blocks with prefix caching; greedy/no penalties/ignore EOS. Outputs must equal the four-block and same-capacity serial controls with correct cleanup. This is CPU structural verification, not a GPU owner or numerical fixture. See t45-mixed-phase-pressure-repair.md.
